humanities_role_explanation: The benchmark targets disciplinary competence in art history, specifically the identification and interpretation of Christian iconography and saint attributes based on the specialized Iconclass classification system, rather than general-purpose object classification.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Multimodal classification tasks pairing artwork images of paintings with candidate class label strings or detailed iconographic textual descriptions.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Single-label image classification of religious artworks. It requires visual recognition of symbolic attributes (e.g., keys, wheels, books), iconographic interpretation of saint identities, and cultural reasoning of Christian religious themes, framed as a closed-set selection (multiple-choice QA).

general_purpose_benchmark.note: The evaluation framework is domain-specific, focusing exclusively on the task of Christian iconography classification.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates state-of-the-art multimodal LLMs including GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Gemini 2.5 Flash.

quantitative_metrics.note: Evaluates using Top-1 accuracy and cross-dataset consistency (measured via block-based image hashing).

summary: This paper presents a benchmarking study of Vision-Language Models and Multimodal Large Language Models on single-label Christian iconography classification. Using subsets of ArtDL, ICONCLASS, and Wikidata, the authors evaluate how zero-shot and few-shot performance is affected by prompt configuration, specifically comparing plain labels with rich Iconclass descriptions.
key_findings: Gemini 2.5 Pro and GPT-4o achieved the highest overall accuracies, peaking at 90.45% and 88.20% respectively on ArtDL, comfortably outperforming fine-tuned ResNet50 baselines. However, on the more heterogeneous Wikidata dataset, SigLIP-SO400M outperformed the LLMs with an accuracy of 66.29%, indicating that contrastive architectures are more robust to inconsistent image sizes and metadata. Enriching prompts with iconographic descriptions generally boosted zero-shot performance, whereas few-shot prompting with five exemplars surprisingly degraded or barely improved accuracy.
facets_explanation: The benchmark relies on pre-existing metadata from ArtDL, the Iconclass AI Test Set, and Wikidata, where artworks are natively mapped to structured Iconclass codes. Answering correctly requires external domain knowledge of the Christian iconographic tradition to link visual attributes (like keys, wheels, or arrows) to specific saintly identities. The evaluation enforces a single correct target label per image by explicitly filtering out multi-label entries, and does not discuss annotator divergence or alternative interpretations.
